record_identity.title: Meta AI users reportedly published sensitive chatbot conversations without fully realising they were public

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Meta AI Discover inadvertent public-chat disclosure
incident_identity.date_basis: AI Incident Database uses 29 April 2025, the Meta AI app launch date, as the Incident date; public reporting of inadvertent disclosures followed in the subsequent weeks.

summary: Meta's standalone AI app included a Discover feed through which users could publish chatbot conversations. Reporting found sensitive medical, legal, relationship, audio and identifying information publicly visible, while some users appeared not to understand that their shared conversations would be public. Meta maintained that publishing required an affirmative share action.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: AIID aggregates multiple reports documenting sensitive conversations visible in Meta AI's Discover feed. TechCrunch reported that users had to press a share control and preview a post before publishing, but said the app did not clearly indicate privacy settings or the destination/public visibility at posting time. The evidence therefore supports user-state confusion rather than automatic publication of every conversation.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence concerns a materially ambiguous transition between private chatbot interaction and public social publication. Distinct privacy/access states existed, but the publication workflow reportedly failed to make the resulting public state sufficiently clear to some users.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The event is a useful non-OpenAI example of access-state governance in conversational AI: social sharing can transform intimate AI interactions into public content, requiring explicit state transitions, audience visibility and privacy signalling.
assessment_boundaries: Meta stated that sharing was opt-in and the evidence does not show that ordinary unshared chats were automatically public.
The number of users who misunderstood the publication state is not established.
VIGIL does not infer that every public Discover post was inadvertent.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Some Meta AI users reportedly shared sensitive chatbot conversations through a Discover workflow without clearly understanding the destination or public visibility.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A transition from private conversation to public publication must make the resulting access state and audience legible before the user commits the change.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The workflow contained a share action and preview, but reportedly failed to communicate the materially different public state clearly enough for some users to understand the exposure.
